steps.message:
I looked before editing, and this hits a contract boundary — flagging before I touch it.

`routes/users.js:6` is the only `userId` in the repo, so the code change is one line. But the README states:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

Renaming in place breaks every existing consumer that reads `userId` — including shipped iOS builds that can't be updated in lockstep, and the nightly partner export. The repo's own stated policy is that this goes through a versioned endpoint.

So I need your call before editing.

questions.question: `GET /users` has external consumers (web, shipped iOS 3.2+, nightly partner export) and the README says field renames go through a versioned endpoint. How should I handle the userId -> user_id rename?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside userId in the existing response. Nothing breaks; consumers migrate at their own pace and userId is removed in a later cleanup. Slightly redundant payload in the interim.
options.preview: users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, user_id: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email }))

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README policy: keep /users as-is and add a v2 route that returns user_id. Largest change (new route, wiring, docs) but the only option matching the stated contract process.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Do exactly what was asked: change userId to user_id in the existing response. Breaks the web app, shipped iOS clients, and the partner export until each is updated.
